name: GIOG
description: Giog is a Malaysian multi-trick game played with Xiangqi pieces used like hidden cards, where players lead valid single or multi-piece combinations and capture tricks with the highest combination of the led type.

content.text: Giog is a Malaysian multi-trick game played with Xiangqi pieces used like hidden cards, where players lead valid single or multi-piece combinations and capture tricks with the highest combination of the led type.
Giog is a Malaysian version of a game played with Chinese chess pieces used as playing-cards, with related forms across China and Southeast Asian Chinese communities.
Base game is typically four players, with adapted procedures for three and two.
32 Xiangqi pieces (16 red, 16 black) ranked from red general down to black pawn in base Giog.
Xiangqi pieces and optional racks for concealed hand management.

Pieces are mixed face down into paired stacks. Players reveal selected bottom pieces to establish priority order, then draft stacks around the layout to form hands (8 pieces each in four-player game).

items.text: Ju Ma Pao: Related Malaysian form with circular two-piece stacks and modified combination set, including general+marshal as highest pair.
Sang Krip: Variant with different distribution and reveal procedure where non-beating plays may remain concealed under winning stacks.
Da Qi Luo: Northeast China versions for 2-5 players with adjusted removal/distribution and alternate combination-ranking systems.
